## What Problem This Solves

Sub-agent approvals currently exist only on their source runtime surfaces. Parent and orchestrator operators cannot opt into a sanitized lifecycle stream, and reconnecting clients have no authoritative pending replay.

Related to #103505. Stacked on #103912.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add an opt-in `session.approval` projection for exact source and persisted ancestor audience keys.
- Keep approval routing observational: no transcript rows, `sessions.changed` events, agent turns, or wakeups.
- Filter every live event and replay row through the approval record's reviewer authorization.
- Return a bounded, authoritative pending replay with filtered keyset scanning so hidden records cannot starve visible ones or distort `truncated`.

- Close the replay/live handoff gap by subscribing before the snapshot and restoring the exact prior subscription if replay setup fails.
- Generate typed Swift session-approval models and status-specific terminal reason enums from the protocol source of truth.

Control UI and native clients can subscribe one session stream and observe sanitized pending/terminal approval truth raised by that session or its descendants. A reconnect receives the current pending set, while first-answer-wins resolution and record-level reviewer binding remain enforced by the canonical approval service.

target.body:
Related: #103505

Stacked on #103679. Review this branch from `codex/approval-typed-actions`.

## What Problem This Solves

Approval prompts currently require the operator to remain on the surface that raised them. Even after the durable approval registry and typed channel actions, OpenClaw has no stable, mobile-friendly document that can be opened directly and refreshed to recover canonical approval state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a standalone authenticated `${controlUiBasePath}/approve/{approvalId}` Control UI document backed by `approval.get` and `approval.resolve`. The Gateway reserves the one-segment approval namespace before plugins and static-file heuristics, including asset-like IDs, and fails closed with 404 when Control UI serving is disabled.

The document is bound to the Gateway that served it. It does not copy or overwrite the full app's saved remote-Gateway selection; URL/session authentication remains ephemeral until an operator explicitly confirms a different Gateway. Approval IDs are decoded once, credentials never enter the approval URL, and terminal state always comes from the SQLite-backed canonical record.

Resolution returns committed SQLite truth before best-effort channel, push, and legacy-event follow-up. A slow or failed secondary surface therefore cannot delay the winning response or replace its result.

## User Impact

Operators can open a stable approval link on a phone or desktop, authenticate, inspect the sanitized command or plugin preview, and approve or deny. Concurrent answers show `Approved here` on the winner and `Resolved elsewhere` with the recorded canonical decision on losers. Reload, reconnect, expiry, cancellation, malformed data, and unavailable approvals all fail closed without usable decision controls.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators using the Android, iPhone, or Apple Watch apps cannot reliably review the same Gateway approval that is visible in the Control UI or a chat channel. Lost acknowledgements can leave a native card looking actionable or resolved without canonical proof, and switching Gateways can misroute stale approval state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This fourth stacked increment makes the official mobile clients read and resolve the durable Gateway approval record. Android and iPhone use the kind-aware unified RPCs, Watch relays reviewer-safe exec prompts through its paired iPhone, and every client treats Gateway terminal state as authoritative. Shipped Gateway v4 peers retain a narrow exec-method fallback; cross-surface retained terminal truth requires the unified methods.

## User Impact

Authorized operators can review pending exec approvals from Android, iPhone, or Apple Watch. The first answer from any authorized surface wins, every native surface displays that recorded result, and a lost response or reconnect cannot silently fabricate approval success or reopen execution rights.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

## What Problem This Solves

#103579 merged with its pre-rebase head, so main is missing the follow-up hardening that closed the review findings on the durable approval registry: the public plugin-sdk d.ts graph still materializes the ProtocolSchemas registry (DTS budget risk), cross-surface approval review is requester-locked (breaking first-answer-wins from a second device), and plugin node.invoke approvals fail open when a presentation is unrenderable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebases the reviewed follow-up delta onto the merged state as one commit so the remaining approval stack (#103679 → #103932) can land on a sound base.

- gateway-protocol wire types derive from owner-module schema consts (`types.ts` tombstone) and `ProtocolSchemas` leaves the package index so public d.ts graphs tree-shake the registry declaration
- approval access authority follows the `operator.approvals` scope tier with `reviewerDeviceIds` as the opt-in restriction; requester identity gates only legacy adapters
- plugin node.invoke approvals register directly so unrenderable presentations throw before request routing
- exec-approval manager reconciliation with the #103515 revocation hardening (resolution source attribution, one-shot ask-fallback consumption)
- surface-report pins, plugin-sdk API baseline, and Swift protocol models refreshed

## User Impact

Approvals requested from one paired device can be reviewed and resolved from any other device holding the approvals scope (Watch/iPhone/Telegram cross-surface flow); plugin-gated node commands deny instead of proceeding when their approval prompt cannot be rendered.

## Evidence

- Testbox build green: `Public plugin SDK declaration graph: 5014292/5050000 bytes`, no forbidden registry declaration (tbx_01kx9sjheam1zb2h5dg27dfhfj)
- `src/gateway/operator-approvals-client.e2e.test.ts` first-answer-wins passes (was `approval not found` before the access fix)
- `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts` fail-closed suite 56/56

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> compaction regression coverage passing (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` -> 56 passed (adds the `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` unit coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector now parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting); both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`); and every version-fallback detector that recognizes an older gateway rejecting an additive field now accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording, so the delimiter change does not silently break mixed-version fallbacks.

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector proof drives the real shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` and the real `requestSessionsUsage` retry path from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; then take the patched formatter's own JSON-quoted rejection, run it through both the old single-quoted matching form and the new shared matcher, and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording to observe whether the additive field is stripped and the call retried.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true

$ node --import tsx proof-detector.mts   # drives real matcher + requestSessionsUsage retry
patched producer message = "invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property \"timeZone\""

# BEFORE (shipped detector: single-quoted includes only):
  matches patched producer output? = false  <- version fallback silently stops firing

# AFTER (shared messageReportsUnexpectedProperty, both wordings):
  matches legacy single-quoted rejection? = true
  matches JSON-quoted rejection?          = true

# real requestSessionsUsage retry against an older gateway:
  legacy single-quoted rejection -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  JSON-quoted rejection          -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  unrelated invalid-usage error   -> rethrown, not retried
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name; and the version-fallback detectors now recognize the patched validator's JSON-quoted rejection that the shipped single-quoted matcher missed, so the real `requestSessionsUsage` strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against an older gateway in both wordings, while an unrelated invalid-usage error is still rethrown without a retry.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook, validation-formatter, and version-fallback-detector layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation set path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins for geolocation set operations with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

The clear path intentionally returns before parsing `origin`, because clearing geolocation and permissions does not use an origin. This preserves existing clients that send stale or malformed origin fields while clearing state.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response for set operations instead of reaching the browser mutation path. `clear=true` still clears geolocation even when an unused origin field is malformed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4c82a884ebec97d3d4a22b79e072fdc9697a4c76`.

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 2 files / 25 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- The route-level `/set/geolocation` proof exercises the registered Browser route handler with the Playwright geolocation adapter mocked at the plugin boundary.
- It proves a supplied page URL, `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`, is normalized before the adapter call, and Playwright receives `origin: "https://geo.example"`.
- It proves `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed set origins return 400 before tab resolution and before any Playwright geolocation call.
- It proves `clear=true` returns before parsing unused coordinates or origin, so malformed unused origin input cannot block geolocation clearing; the adapter receives `clear: true` for the selected tab.
- The sibling `/permissions/grant` route proof remains in the focused run to show the shared HTTP(S) origin parser keeps permission-origin behavior aligned.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

target.title: fix(plugins): keep API key preview from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the API-key preview shown during provider setup could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the pasted key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatApiKeyPreview` used raw `String.prototype.slice` for its head and tail snippets, which can cut through surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the redacted preview always stays on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The change is limited to this display helper and its test.

## User Impact

Setup confirmation prompts and status output that display API-key previews remain well-formed when the key value contains non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/plugins/provider-auth-input.test.ts` covering ASCII redaction and astral boundary cases.
- Existing provider auth input tests continue to pass.
- Fixed a test callback that passed `Array.map`'s numeric index as the formatter's `opts` argument; it now uses an explicit unary wrapper.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, `formatApiKeyPreview("a😀b")` returned `"a\ud83d…\ude00b"` (isolated surrogate halves at both edges). After the patch it returns `"a…b"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/provider-auth-preview-utf16` at `c5ea197606ae06c8b1dc4700c2781667360cb5b8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; for (const v of ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]) console.log(JSON.stringify(formatApiKeyPreview(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the previews survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "pv-")), "p.txt"); const samples = ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]; const previews = samples.map((value) => formatApiKeyPreview(value)); writeFileSync(f, previews.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === previews.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "a…b"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "😀😀…😀😀"

  a…b
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  😀😀…😀😀
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at preview boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every preview, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined previews survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live provider setup flow; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

After stabilizing request shape, numeric-only records from a long-lived room session show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens; the final four turns reused 98.7-99.2% of the input prefix. Exact-head isolated live-provider probes then reused 40,960 cached tokens on warm GPT-5.5 turns (99.5%) and 40,448 on warm GPT-5.6 turns (98.2-98.3%), with one stable 48-tool ordered shape digest. No transcript text or private identifiers are included.

## Root Cause

Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;
3. built-in authenticated OpenAI Responses streams could miss native `previous_response_id` continuation.

## Expected Contract

- One stable model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue for a session.
- One deterministic, trusted current-turn `ToolAccessPolicy` enforced before side effects.
- Trusted-internal capability remains distinct from owner identity, so limited core-tool grants cannot expose owner-only plugin tools.
- Actual reply routing remains turn-specific without changing prompt-facing tool shape.
- Queue, memory, compaction, provider, and recovery boundaries preserve the same state.
- Authenticated GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Responses use native continuation; custom streams retain their routing.
- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

## Candidate Fix

PR #102189 at `b0a9bfc589f8deff1ed9dd5345276093d6df25b2` implements the contract above.

The candidate includes upstream `7027d2c227281d814266311bebab7581b899d6dc` and has a clean merge-tree check against it. Pre-refresh broad validation passed 2,446 changed-file tests plus focused trusted-internal ownership, compaction, overflow recovery, harness selection, and manual propagation coverage. Exact-head validation passes 14 proof assertions across 18 suites, 215 Codex lifecycle/binding/login-profile tests, production typecheck, prompt snapshots, diff checks, and a full build.

An exact-head focused proof run passes 14 selected assertions across 18 suites: strict room-event delivery, pre-hook/pre-side-effect denial, permitted trusted-internal execution, and GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 `previous_response_id` delta continuation.

The exact commit is installed on the reporter's local gateway: OpenClaw `2026.7.2`, LaunchAgent loaded, runtime active, connectivity probe OK, dashboard HTTP 200, Discord probe OK, WhatsApp linked/healthy, and build-info commit matches the candidate.

## Privacy

Evidence is intentionally sanitized. No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter.

target.body:
## Summary

Phase 0 of MCP Apps support (the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension implemented by Claude and ChatGPT): OpenClaw's bundle MCP client detects tools that declare interactive `ui://` resources on **any configured MCP server**, fetches the app document after the tool call, and the Control UI renders it in a sandboxed iframe with a minimal MCP Apps postMessage host. Plugins can attach MCP App servers declaratively via a new `mcpServers` manifest field for native plugins.

No server-specific integration is bundled. The official [Excalidraw MCP App server](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw-mcp) served as the proof of concept and lives out of tree as an external plugin ([fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin)); any spec-conforming server works via `mcp.servers.<name>` config or the plugin manifest field.

**Draft because of one known blocker** (found by Codex review, confirmed empirically): `about:srcdoc` iframes inherit the embedding page's CSP, and the gateway-served Control UI ships `script-src 'self'` (`src/gateway/control-ui-csp.ts`), which blocks inline app scripts before they can initialize. The inline preview therefore only functions on CSP-less deployments (e.g. dev servers) today. The fix — serving app documents from a dedicated ticketed route with per-app CSP headers (the spec's sandbox-proxy pattern) — is the planned Phase 1 host work; this module's bridge, sizing, registry, and all server-side plumbing carry over unchanged. Everything else in the PR (capability negotiation, `_meta.ui` parsing, visibility enforcement, resource fetch, plugin-declared MCP servers, text fallback) works on production deployments now.

## What's in here

**Server side (`src/agents`)**
- Bundle MCP client declares `capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"]` (`mimeTypes: ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]`).
- `src/agents/mcp-apps.ts`: parses tool `_meta.ui` (nested + deprecated flat `ui/resourceUri` key) and app resources from `resources/read` results (text/blob, CSP + permissions metadata, 5MB cap). All treated as untrusted server output.
- App-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `"model"`, including explicitly empty lists) never materialize as agent tools.
- After a ui-bearing tool call succeeds, the runtime reads the `ui://` resource and attaches `{ resource, toolInput, result }` as `details.mcpApp` on the tool result. Failures degrade to the plain text result. Tool input is persisted in details because durable transcripts split calls and results into separate messages.

**Control UI (`ui/src`)**
- `details.mcpApp` becomes a `kind: "mcp-app"` tool-card preview rendered in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` srcdoc iframe (never `allow-same-origin`), with the app-declared CSP inserted structurally via DOMParser and origin expressions validated before interpolation.
- Minimal host bridge: answers `ui/initialize` (protocol `2026-01-26`), pushes `ui/notifications/tool-input` / `tool-result` (incl. `_meta`) after `initialized`, handles `size-changed` and `ping`, and fails fast with JSON-RPC method-not-found for requests Phase 0 does not service (`tools/call`, `ui/open-link`, …) so apps degrade instead of hanging.
- Frames register synchronously via lit `ref()` (srcdoc scripts can post before `load`) and unregister on detach.

**Plugin surface (`src/plugins`)**
- Native (`format: "openclaw"`) plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers` — same shape as `mcp.servers.<name>` config, merged through the existing enabled-bundle path. User config still wins by server name; `enabled: false` detaches a plugin-declared server. Documented in `docs/plugins/manifest.md`.

**Docs**
- Generic MCP Apps behavior/limits section in `docs/cli/mcp.md`; `mcpServers` field in the plugin manifest reference.

## Verification

- Live against `mcp.excalidraw.com` (configured via `mcp.servers`, exercising only the generic path): capability handshake accepted; app-only tools (`export_to_excalidraw`, `save_checkpoint`, `read_checkpoint`) filtered from the materialized tool list; `create_view` produced `details.mcpApp` with the real 432KB `text/html;profile=mcp-app` document and `csp: { connectDomains: ["https://esm.sh"], resourceDomains: ["https://esm.sh"] }`.
- Browser (no-CSP page): the real Excalidraw app booted inside the sandboxed srcdoc iframe under the generated CSP, completed `ui/initialize` → `initialized` → tool-input/tool-result, drew the diagram, and its `size-changed` notifications resized the frame.
- Browser (Control-UI-equivalent CSP header): confirmed the inherited-CSP blocker — iframe mounts, app never boots (hence draft + documented limitation).
- `vitest`: new suites for `_meta.ui`/resource parsing, preview extraction, native-manifest MCP server merge; adjacent suites (tool cards, manifest registry, plugin contracts, loader) all green. `tsgo` core/ui/extensions typechecks clean; `pnpm lint` and `oxfmt` clean.

## Review

Three Codex autoreview rounds (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) on the branch diff. Fixed across rounds: frame-registration race ahead of srcdoc execution, `visibility: []` model-exposure bypass, lost tool input on transcript reload, CSP origin-expression injection, regex head-insertion bypass (now DOMParser), `base-uri` honoring `baseUriDomains`, `_meta` passthrough, and detached-frame retention. Escalated rather than patched: the srcdoc CSP-inheritance blocker above (architecture change → Phase 1) and app-initiated `tools/call` proxying (deliberately out of Phase 0 scope; documented as view-only).

Note: `docs/plugins/reference/anthropic.md` is stale against the inventory generator on current `main` (pre-existing; `node scripts/generate-plugin-inventory-doc.mjs --check` fails on a clean checkout). Not touched here.

Configuring `session.maintenance.pruneAfter: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolvePruneAfterMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `pruneStaleEntries` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 30d default applies; positive durations and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +198/-1)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +17: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +118: 14 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  12 passed (12)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.pruneAfter",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.pruneAfter is a zero duration — this causes
immediate deletion of all sessions. Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to
remove it so the documented 30d default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.pruneAfter "0h" (zero duration);
documented 30d default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## What Problem This Solves

Normal safeguard auto-compaction still registers the active session model even when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` selects a different summarization target. Main's new route-aware auth planner fixed explicit compaction, but normal safeguard registration still ignored the override.

A safeguard override also needs its model route and credential to remain one atomic tuple. Binding a target credential into the active attempt registry can corrupt same-provider sessions before compaction starts.

## Summary

This refresh is merged with main at `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756` and adapts the safeguard override to the current route-aware runtime planner.

- Resolve the configured safeguard target before synchronous extension registration.
- Reuse an existing prepared auth plan only when it exactly matches the target provider/model.
- Otherwise prepare the target through the atomic runtime flow:
  `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` → `materializePreparedRuntimeModel` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeAuthAttempts` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeModelAuth`.
- Preserve the selected model route, auth requirement, request transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and credential as one tuple.
- Resolve the target with an isolated `AuthStorage`/`ModelRegistry`; never mutate the active attempt's auth registry.
- Carry the prepared model, target registry, and resolved auth plan through the safeguard runtime registry.
- Prefer the prepared safeguard model and its paired registry in the hook.
- Reject prepared routes whose runtime policy does not support the OpenClaw runtime.
- Preserve locked native-harness sessions on their pinned model.
- Warn and fall back to the active model when the configured target cannot be resolved or authenticated.
- Keep explicit compaction on main's current prepared-route implementation while forwarding its resolved model, registry, and auth plan into safeguard runtime state.

## Safety Invariants

- A same-provider override using a different profile cannot replace the active session key.
- Cross-provider model, API, base URL, route requirement, transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key are resolved together.
- The safeguard hook looks up target credentials in the target registry, not the active attempt registry.
- `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` remains synchronous by receiving a precomputed target.

## Evidence

Validated on exact local tree `b38eded0065419c75b3b1f369b96d7359c0cb239`:

- PR head: `9f2ac5d5ac9e17d20e9ec7be684f82157b4b3327`
- Merge parents: prior PR head `ecfc4491ece04b29ccb48c42ecb6a40d6e0d8a37` and main `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756`
- Diff from merged main: 9 files, +1022/-21
- Core production TypeScript — passed
- Core test TypeScript — passed
- Planner/safeguard focused suites — 238 tests passed
- Compaction context/resource-loader suites — 62 tests passed
- Duplicate extension-project coverage — 26 tests passed
- Concrete OpenAI route regression asserts API, base URL, auth requirement, request overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key
- Same-provider alternate-profile regression proves target-key isolation from the active registry
- `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` — passed
- Independent semantic review confirmed the adapted diff preserves main's atomic route/auth contract

A direct compact-hooks subset currently reproduces 9/102 failures on an unmodified `266d49c` worktree as well as the merge tree; the conflicted compact implementation and harness are byte-identical to main. No unrelated main fix is included here. Fresh exact-head GitHub CI is running.

## Testing Scope

No live provider API call was made. Exact-head automated coverage proves route/auth tuple integrity and active-registry isolation. A real provider-backed automatic cross-provider safeguard compaction remains an external maintainer/environment proof gate.

target.title: Propagate AbortSignal through bundle MCP tool/resource/prompt calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run is cancelled, pending bundle MCP tool/resource/prompt requests keep running because the per-call `AbortSignal` is dropped after `AgentTool.execute`. This leaves MCP child work alive after the caller has aborted, wastes resources, and can produce late results that race with cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #104110 fixed the same issue for bundle LSP JSON-RPC requests by forwarding the `AbortSignal` and emitting `$/cancelRequest`. Bundle MCP uses the same `AgentTool.execute` contract but ignores the signal all the way down to the MCP SDK client. This change plumbs the signal through the same layers so MCP requests can be cancelled.

## User Impact

- Cancelling an agent turn or session now stops pending bundle MCP tool calls, resource reads, and prompt fetches instead of letting them run to completion.
- Reduces wasted compute and prevents late MCP responses from being applied after cancellation.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` that verifies the `AbortSignal` is forwarded from each projected tool's `execute` into `runtime.callTool`, `listResources`, `readResource`, `listPrompts`, and `getPrompt`.
- Existing tests pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` → 57 tests passed across 2 shards.
  - `npx oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` → clean.
  - `npx oxlint src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts` → clean.
- Minimal scope: only touches bundle MCP runtime/types/materialize + one focused test file.

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

## Real behavior proof

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
